title: Horae Hebraicae et Talmudicae (A Commentary on the New Testament from the Talmud and Hebraica)
author: John Lightfoot
summary: A Puritan Hebraist's notes on the Gospels and Acts from Jewish sources; on Matthew 24 he reads the darkened heavens and the passing of heaven and earth as the end of the Jewish state in AD 70.
note: Public-domain work, cited by the passage commented on; no specific online edition checked.

title: Through New Eyes: Developing a Biblical View of the World
author: James B. Jordan
summary: Biblical-theology study of the symbolic world of Scripture, arguing that each major covenant brought a new 'heavens and earth' with new rulers and a new sanctuary.

title: A New Testament Biblical Theology: The Unfolding of the Old Testament in the New
author: G. K. Beale
summary: Presents the New Testament storyline as the 'already and not yet' new-creational kingdom begun in Christ's resurrection and completed at his return.

title: The Temple and the World (The Journal of Religion 64:3)
author: Jon D. Levenson
summary: Jewish biblical scholar's study of how the Jerusalem temple was understood in Israel as a small model of the created world.

title: Worldview and Textual Criticism in 2 Peter 3:10 (Westminster Theological Journal 49)
author: Al Wolters
summary: Argues that the earliest reading of 2 Peter 3:10, 'will be found', points to a purging and renewal of the earth rather than its annihilation.

title: Beyond Creation Science: New Covenant Creation from Genesis to Revelation
author: Timothy P. Martin and Jeffrey L. Vaughn
summary: Sets out the covenant-creation reading, which takes the 'heavens and earth' of Genesis 1 as the covenant world that passed away in AD 70; a minority view even among preterists.

title: On the Life of Moses, Book 2
author: Philo of Alexandria
summary: First-century Jewish philosopher who, like Josephus, read the tabernacle furnishings and the high priest's robes as symbols of the cosmos.
note: Primary ancient text, cited by standard section numbers.

title: Discourses and Sayings of Our Lord Jesus Christ
author: John Brown of Edinburgh
summary: Scottish expositor who read the passing of heaven and earth in Matthew 5:18 as Old Testament language for the end of the Mosaic economy.
